To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
young, premenopausal women are at higher than average risk of developing gastric pouch distension after laparoscopic gastric banding.
women younger than 50 years of age are at higher risk than older women or men for developing proximal gastric pouch dilation after adjustable gastric banding.
younger women were more at risk of PPD than men and women over the age of 50.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of gastric pouch enlargement following laparoscopic adjustable banding (LAG).
the influence of age (and gender) on the development of PPD after gastric banding surgery.
the influence of sex hormones on the development of PPD after adjustable gastric banding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
women of a younger age are at a higher risk of PPS than men and women of an older age, and that the risk of PPD in women is higher in the premenopausal state.
younger women are at higher risks of PPD after laparoscopic gastric banding surgery than men and older women.
younger women are at higher than average risk of PPD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
women, especially younger women, are more prone to gastric pouch enlargement and that this may be a consequence of sex hormones.
younger women have an increased risk of PPD, which may be due to hormonal influences.
women younger than 50 years are at increased risk of pouch distension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
young women may be at higher risk of complications from LAGB surgery and may require closer surveillance and follow-up.
women are at a higher risk of gastric pouch enlargement and that this risk is highest for women under the age of 40.
